report.root_cause: AuditTrail plugin config (plugins/AuditTrail/config.yml) was changed to debug: true at about 07:15:21; the reload at 07:15:22 enabled debug tracing, which wrote plugins/AuditTrail/debug/trace-0.log at roughly 1 MB/s (about 52 MB, with trace-1.log at about 19.5 MB by the time it was stopped) on the 443 MB server volume. I did not identify who made the change.
report.actions: 1. Checked status and logs: TPS 20, disk growing from 23 MB to 80 MB within about a minute. 2. Ran fs_du: found plugins/AuditTrail/debug/trace-0.log (41-52 MB). 3. Log showed "AuditTrail config reloaded (debug=true)" at 07:15:22. 4. Read plugins/AuditTrail/config.yml (debug: true, retention-days: 30). 5. Wrote plugins/AuditTrail/config.yml with debug: false and retention-days: 30 (unchanged). 6. Log confirmed "AuditTrail config reloaded (debug=false)" at 07:15:40. 7. Disk growth stopped; stable at 95 MB (22%) for over 90 seconds. 8. Declared incident. Did not delete files, restart the server, or ban anyone.
report.residual_risk: Debug trace files remain on disk: plugins/AuditTrail/debug/trace-0.log (about 52 MB) and trace-1.log (about 19.5 MB), roughly 72 MB total. I left them because I could not confirm they are disposable; an operator should review and remove them. The person or process that enabled debug mode at 07:15 is unknown and should be checked. The plugin reloads config live, so re-enabling debug would recur the same fill. I declared the incident after the fix rather than the moment growth was first noticed.
